paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Ella asked a really important question: how is emptiness an unchanging thing?

Unchanging does not mean forever. This is hard. Some translations of *takpa* [`RTAG PA`] and *mitakpa* [`MI RTAG PA`] say *takpa* [`RTAG PA`] means permanent, and *mitakpa* [`MI RTAG PA`] means not permanent. That’s a bad translation in most cases.
We say *takpa* [`RTAG PA`] is unchanging. *Mitakpa* [`MI RTAG PA`] is changing.
It’s interesting in Tibetan. If you look at it, unchanging means not changing. It’s a negative.
I’m going to draw you a picture on the screen.

Here is *mitakpa* [`MI RTAG PA`]. This is when something starts. Imagine you’re born here. You grow up, you grow up, you grow up. You reach your fifties, sixties, seventies, depending on where you are. Eventually your body wears out and you’re done.
That’s a changing thing. It starts and it ends. Because it was born, it has to die.

Now, this straight line represents emptiness. Every object has that. The emptiness of your body is always the same. There’s never more or less emptiness. However, the moment your body ends, your body stops, and the emptiness stops too. Your body dies; the emptiness stops as well. But we don’t say “stops.” It just goes away.

Emptiness is consistent. It doesn’t change. There’s never more or less emptiness. Emptiness doesn’t start; emptiness doesn’t end. The body doesn’t start and doesn’t end either, but that’s a different story.
This requires meditation. You just have to think about it.

This cup has emptiness. The emptiness never changes. It’s always one hundred percent empty. Empty of what? Empty of coming from its own side. Empty of not coming from you providing cups to other people. This is a bad example, but I couldn’t think of another one.
This pen is empty of me providing good communication to other people, because this is the communication tool. Maybe it’s empty of me being clear with other people in my communication.

That’s what emptiness means. I think the problem is with the word, because words are empty. The word “emptiness” has emptiness. The sound “emptiness,” the syllables coming out of Tim’s mouth, are not emptiness.

Think of it when we do Adam’s text, when we do *chi jedrak* [`SPYI BYE BRAG`]: the mental image and the specific thing. The mental image and the car. The Toyota, and car. Really think about *chi* [`SPYI`] as the straight line, and the Toyota as the specific car.

Someone’s going to argue with me, and that’s okay. We’re in the logic schools. Is it completely accurate? Maybe, maybe not. We’ve been debating this for ages. Is the mental image unchanging? This is why the logic schools are fun.
If you can take that into your meditations, what would it mean if the *chi* [`SPYI`] is unchanging and the *jedrak* [`BYE BRAG`] is changing? What would it mean? Is Tim correct from its own side?
What would it mean not to die? You have to break those words down. You have to break down which part of what you’re saying is self-existent.

chapters.title: Why Mixed Nuts trains the mind across schools

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Thank you all for joining. Our hour is up. I don’t want to keep you all forever.
This is what we’re doing in the Mixed Nuts. I’ve been doing this for four or five years now. It’s like being dunked in water. You’re forcing yourself to be thrown into the ocean of misunderstanding.

In literally every Mixed Nuts class, you think, “You’ve got to be kidding me. Really? I don’t understand anything.” I really questioned this idea: why do we do five texts every day? As soon as you feel like you understand something, it’s like, “Let’s go over to *Abhidharma* now. Let’s go over to Mind Only.” It drives me nuts.
But it really helps your mind be able to jump between different schools like that. How does it help you when you’re helping other people?

If you can understand, when someone is talking to you about their problems, what’s going to help them? Is the holodeck in the *kunshi* [`KUN GZHI`] going to help them? Is the *Abhidharma* going to help them? Is Lower Middle Way going to help them?

You need to understand the differences, because really the differences are just your mind projecting them anyway. The people presenting their problems to you are just your seeds anyway, stuck in the *Abhidharma*. It’s just your mind and your seeds projecting a person who’s stuck in an *Abhidharma* worldview.

So whose fault is it anyway? You might as well learn it. Become friends with it. Become friends with the Vinaya. Become friends with logic. Become friends with the holodeck in your *kunshi* [`KUN GZHI`], with the *kunshi* [`KUN GZHI`] as the holodeck. Become friends with the Diamond Cutter Sutra.

Then you become an amazing teacher. I don’t mean, “I’m going to sit on Zoom and teach people.” I mean you go off and make friends with everyone in your world. You become the mayor of your town—not political mayor. Everywhere you go, you’re helping people, and people feel it. People sense it. You’re asking the question, “What can I do for you?”

I’m going to go take a nap. Thanks for your great questions today. That was awesome. That was really cool. If anyone wants to work on a four-step karmic program to create more time in the world, let me know.
Have a lovely day. Thank you. See you tonight.
